brief: Goldman's morning note compiles four pieces. US Economics forecasts August core CPI at 0.23% month over month against 0.2% consensus, 2.40% year over year, and headline 0.39% on higher energy, which implies a 0.22% core PCE increase, revised up to 24bp after PPI airfares and medical care came in stronger. Shelter and autos are benign, airfares rise 4.0%, and core runs near 0.2% for the next couple of months unless oil disruptions persist. Short macro trading argues the Fed is now hostage to this one print: Waller was overtly dovish, a 30bp core reading merits a hike, the market's over/under is 25bp, and with over 50% hike probability priced, a hold risks being read as a policy error. Cole pays the October Fed meeting, expects European front-end flatteners after the ECB's hawkish repricing, treats consecutive BoJ hikes as a high hurdle so receives the first three meetings, and criticises Treasury buybacks being tethered to yield levels. Europe Economics recaps a 25bp ECB hike, now forecasts a further 25bp in December to 2.75%, cuts pushed to 2027Q4, terminal nudged to 2.25%. Energy prices rose, Brent above $95 and TTF above EUR70/MwH.
